_help: Policy knobs for the customer_support persona (Lumen Cloud). Strictest signal wins: BLOCK > HOLD_FOR_REVIEW > APPROVE.
on_ezio_failure_why: If Ezio cannot be reached we fail closed to a human review, because an unsent email costs minutes while a wrong one costs trust.
tier_decisions_why: GREEN may send only if our own price and policy checks also pass, YELLOW needs a person, and RED means Ezio found a serious problem so it never goes to a customer.

tone.why: Ezio marks tone under 60 as critical; one friendly '!' or an acronym like GDPR only costs 6 to 10 points, so 60 holds real hype without holding normal replies.

bias.why: Each one-sided marker ('clearly', 'only way') costs 15 points, so under 80 means two or more and the email is pushing the customer instead of informing them.

agreement.why: Any flattery or 'you're absolutely right' drops agreement below 80, and our rules say flattery and agreeing with a customer's claim go to a manager.

when_accuracy_not_scored_why: Ezio cannot see our price sheet, so 'not scored' is normal; our own source-of-truth check covers those facts.
when_accuracy_unavailable_why: If the public fact-check is down we cannot rule out a wrong legal or regulatory claim, so a person reviews it.
on_unverifiable_claim_why: A public claim Ezio cannot verify is neither safe nor proven wrong, so a person checks it before it reaches a customer.
laya_why: Optional and add-only: on the practice texts real promises scored 0.82 to 0.93 and good emails at most 0.44, so 0.80 holds a likely promise without holding normal replies; it never approves or blocks.
